common.name: Name
notifications.empty: Nothing yet. What Tetra tells you — space freed, a disk filling up, a drive backed up — is kept here.
settings.themeAutoNote: Auto follows the system's light or dark setting.
settings.languageNote: Tetra's words. System default is the system's language, or English when Tetra does not have it yet.
settings.motionRemoveNote: An import leaves out the few seconds of video beside a picture (MVIMG_….MP4 next to MVIMG_….jpg). The picture comes in on its own.
settings.motionAsOneNote: A picture and its few seconds of video show as one photo; the Motion button in the viewer plays them. Pictures with the video inside (Pixel, Samsung) play too.
settings.motionAutoplayOn: A motion photo plays its few seconds as soon as it opens.
settings.motionAutoplayOff: Motion photos open still; the Motion button plays them.
settings.callSoundHere: A call's sound is on this computer: its speakers and microphone.
settings.callSoundPhone: A call's sound stays on the phone. Call, Answer and End in Contacts and the call bubble work either way.
settings.btHowTo: To hear calls here: pair the phone with this computer in the system's Bluetooth settings, then on the phone open Bluetooth › this computer › and allow "Phone calls". Tetra then shows it connected here, and says so when it connects or drops.
settings.btMissing: bluetoothctl is not installed, so Tetra cannot see Bluetooth here.
sync.pairStep1: On the phone open {tetra} and tap {sync}.
sync.pairStep2: Tap {pair} and point the camera at this code.
sync.pairStep3: The phone appears in the list, ready to back up.
sync.ruleOffPhotos: No photos cross, in either direction.
sync.ruleOffFiles: No files cross, in either direction.
sync.ruleBothPhotos: Each side sends the photos the other is missing. Always a copy.
sync.ruleBothFiles: Each side sends the files the other is missing. Always a copy.
sync.moveWindowPhotos: {device} keeps the last {span}; older photos that {here} holds are offered to move off it, into its Trash.
sync.moveWindowPhotosFav: {device} keeps the last {span} and its favorites; older photos that {here} holds are offered to move off it, into its Trash.
sync.moveWindowFiles: {device} keeps the last {span}; older files that {here} holds go to its Trash at each sync.
sync.moveWindowFilesFav: {device} keeps the last {span} and its favorites; older files that {here} holds go to its Trash at each sync.
sync.oldCopy: This was set as a copy before Moves had a window.
sync.reportedName: It reported {name} when it paired. The name is only used here.
sync.selfWordHint: Every rule on this page is written from a device's side, so this is the word on the other end of each of them: {word}.
sync.hub1: Every device pairs with this machine and with nothing else. A phone and a tablet never talk to each other — they each talk to {label}, which is how anything gets from one to the other.
sync.hub2: So: {connect} It is also the only machine that can see the whole picture — what exists, how many copies there are, and what is safe to free — because it is the only one every device reports to.
sync.hubConnect: connect every device to this one.
sync.hub3: It has to be running and on the same network for anything to cross. Nothing is ever deleted by a sync, and a device is only ever {offered} the chance to free space, never told.
sync.whyHead_one: {Here} has never been given these {n} files.
sync.whyHead_other: {Here} has never been given these {n} files.
sync.whyReceive: {head} Its Photos row for {name} is "{here} → {name}", so {name} never offers anything and these will stay where they are until that changes.
sync.whyOff: {head} Photos are switched off for {name}, so nothing crosses in either direction.
sync.whyOther: {head} {name} is allowed to send photos, so these were offered and did not make it across — a failed transfer, or a file Android would not let it read. The device knows which; it does not say yet.
sync.notNamed: not named by the device yet
sync.hintOne: in one place in the world
sync.libraryTitle: The library, and where it is
sync.copiesAria: how many machines hold each file
sync.aloneTitle: Files that exist in one place only
sync.aloneWhy: One machine holds these and nothing else does. Losing that machine loses the file.
sync.madeOfAria: what the library is made of, by size
sync.staleReceipts_one: {n} file was received and checked on {here} and is no longer on disk. They are counted as missing again, so the device that has them will be asked for them on its next sync.
sync.staleReceipts_other: {n} files were received and checked on {here} and are no longer on disk. They are counted as missing again, so the device that has them will be asked for them on its next sync.
sync.libraryNote: Photos only: the Drive folder is a second library with its own manifest, and counting the two together made every number ambiguous. Counted over everything known anywhere, not only what is on {here} — a photo on one phone and nowhere else is the one worth warning about, so it has to be in the picture. Sizes are only known for what {here} holds, so a file that is only on a device is counted and never weighed. {couldFree} is what a device could give back, because every byte of it was read back and checked on {here} — nothing is deleted by a sync, the device would be asked first. Each row is as fresh as that device's last sync.
sync.pairNothingCrosses: Nothing crosses until you have answered what should cross: the new device appears below with every row Off, waiting for that.
sync.addDrivePlugged: A drive that is plugged in
sync.countsAsCopy: It counts as a copy from now on, so anything that lives only on this computer and on that drive shows as two places rather than one.
sync.noDrive: Nothing is plugged in that this app can write to. Connect a drive and open this again.
sync.cannotWrite: This app cannot write to {mount}. Nothing was changed.
sync.notEnoughRoom: There is not enough room: {need} to copy, {free} free.
sync.keepPurgatoryOnSub: deleted items wait there for their last days instead of on this PC; what is in it now moves there
sync.driveFileChanged: A Drive file that changed replaces the drive's copy, and the older one is kept in Tetra/Files history. To let old photos live on it instead of this PC, make it Storage on its card afterwards.
sync.everythingUnder: Everything goes under {path} and nothing else on the drive is touched. Each file is read back and checked after it is written, and nothing is ever deleted or lost — on the drive or here. Nothing crosses until you press Start.
sync.noLongerPlugged: That drive is no longer plugged in.
sync.moveStep1Photos: {device} sends {here} the photos it is missing, each checked on arrival. {Here} stops sending photos to {device}.
sync.moveStep1Files: {device} sends {here} the files it is missing, each checked on arrival. {Here} stops sending files to {device}.
sync.moveStep3Files: Older files that {here} holds go to {device}'s own Trash at each sync — only files; every folder stays, Documents and Scanned Documents included. They wait there their 30 days and then go to the purgatory.
sync.moveStep3Photos: Older photos that {here} holds are offered on {device}'s Sync page to move off it — into its Trash, where they wait their 30 days and then go to the purgatory. Nothing is removed without that tap.
sync.moveStep4: {Here} keeps every one of them, whatever {device} puts in its Trash.
sync.notHereYet: Not on {here} yet — sent first, then counted
sync.notListedPhotos: {name} has not listed its photos yet; the numbers appear after its next sync.
sync.notListedFiles: {name} has not listed its files yet; the numbers appear after its next sync.
sync.moveMeans: A Move means {here} keeps everything and {device} only a window. To keep everything on both, choose Both ways or a Copy instead.
sync.historyHint: Everything that crossed, moved or was deleted, and for which device. Nothing here is ever edited.
sync.thenPurgatory: then in the purgatory on {place} for {days}
sync.purgatoryHowDrive: After its time in the Trash an item is not deleted: it goes to a hidden {folder} folder on the drive, checked byte for byte, and only after that time is it gone. With the drive unplugged it waits in the Trash. Emptying the Trash by hand is a plain delete.
sync.purgatoryHowComputer: After its time in the Trash an item is not deleted: it goes to a hidden {folder} folder on the computer, checked byte for byte, and only after that time is it gone. Tick “Keep the purgatory here” on a drive’s card to keep it there instead. Emptying the Trash by hand is a plain delete.
sync.nowLiveOn: {n} photos now live on {name}. They are still in Photos, People and search; opening one needs {name} plugged in.
sync.nothingToFreeWhy: Every photo {why} that {name} holds has already left this PC, or is a favorite{copies}. A backup to {name} runs by itself while it is plugged in.
sync.orNotInPlaces: , or is not yet in {n} places
sync.readBack: Each one is read back from {name} and checked, and only then is this PC's copy deleted — not put in the Trash, which is on this same disk and would free nothing. They stay in your library: thumbnails, People, collections and search keep them, and they open from {name} whenever it is plugged in.
sync.evenEvery: Even every photo that may go leaves this disk above {pct} %: another {size} is other things on it.
sync.movedWaiting: {moved} moved; {n} wait until the drive they are on is plugged in.
sync.offloadOnNote: keep the disk under a line
sync.keepLastOnPc: Keep the last {n} {unit} on this PC
sync.placesHold_one: place holds it ({name} counts, this PC does not)
sync.placesHold_other: places hold it ({name} counts, this PC does not)
sync.favoritesAlwaysStay: Favorites always stay on this PC
sync.goesByItself: It goes by itself, and you are told.
sync.autoFree: Free space by itself, without asking
sync.keepPurgatoryHereSub: otherwise it stays on this PC
sync.forgetBody: It can no longer send photos until you pair it again. Photos already received stay.
sync.selfChipTitle: What this machine is, and what to call it
sync.hubButtonTitle: What this machine does for the others
sync.notSetUp: Not set up yet — nothing crosses until you say what should. Choose below, then it starts.
sync.listening: Listening on {addresses} · port {port}. Only paired devices can reach it. Every file is checked by SHA-256 on the side that receives it before it is kept, nothing is overwritten, and a sync never deletes anything on either device.
data.tipReachedText: {used} of {size} used, {days} days before the renewal.
data.tipComesText: At your usual pace the {size} run out before {end}. To last, stay near {budget} a day.
data.tipAboutText: At your usual pace you will use about {used} of {size}: {spare} to spare. Up to {budget} a day still makes it.
data.tipHotspotText: Most of the plan goes to the tablet and this computer. Their updates, downloads, backups and video fill it fastest: leave those for a Wi-Fi that is not the phone's, or set them to pause on metered networks (NetworkManager marks the phone's hotspot as metered).
data.tipWeekendsText: A weekend day {weekend}, a workday {workday}: with no Wi-Fi at work to lean on, weekends are where a Wi-Fi saves the most.
data.tipAppText: The app using the most of the plan this cycle, on any of your devices. Its own settings may have a data saver, a lower video quality, or updates on Wi-Fi only.
data.infoRing: The ring: how much of the limit the phone's plan has used this cycle (counting from what you typed from the carrier, if you did). Budget: what is left shared over the days left. Forecast: where your usual days take you by the renewal.
data.setUp: Set Data up on the phone (Data › Setup); its plan and counts come here with sync.
data.infoBars: Each bar is a day of the phone's plan: its own mobile data (lime), what its hotspot shared (orange), Wi-Fi (blue) and Android Auto's link to the car (teal). Apps: the same days by app — the phone's own on mobile and what the tablet's and this computer's took through the hotspot. Faint bars: the days to come, each the median of the same weekday over the last three weeks. Dashed: your average day. Click a bar for its apps.
data.legendNote: · dashed: the average, {avg} a day · faint: the days to come
data.infoCycle: The solid line adds up the plan's data day by day; the dashed one carries it on with your usual days to the renewal; the top line is the limit. If the dashed line crosses it, the limit comes before the renewal.
data.infoNumbers: The phone's mobile data, as the plan counts it. A day: the days so far, today left out. Workdays and weekends: the typical (median) day of each over the last three weeks. Through the hotspot: the share of the mobile data the phone gave to other devices.
data.infoTips: Worked out from your own days: the pace, where the data goes, the weekdays and the apps. Only information — Data changes nothing; each line says where you could change it yourself.
data.clientsNotYet: The tablet's and this computer's counts have not come yet.
data.notCounted: Not counted by them: {size} (a guest, hours they were off, overheads)
data.infoDevices: Each device's own count: the phone's mobile data (its own and what its hotspot shared) and Android Auto's link, the tablet's and this computer's Wi-Fi and what of it went through the phone's hotspot; Ethernet when this computer was on a cable.
data.noLink: This computer is on neither Wi-Fi nor a cable.
phone.tapToCall: The phone shows it: tap to call
phone.spamOn: On the spam list: it will not ring
phone.spamHint: Calls from these are declined on the phone before they ring. A * at the end takes a whole range (69800*).
phone.noCalls: The phone's calls show here once Tetra is the phone's phone app (Settings › Phone on the phone).
phone.lookUp: Look it up on CallInsider (opens the browser)
phone.noFavourites: Star people in Contacts and they show here.
phone.noRecordings: Calls recorded on this computer show here.
phone.padHint: The phone places the call; its sound is on this computer when the phone is connected by Bluetooth (Settings › Calls).
sync.errChanged: It changed on the way; nothing was kept.
sync.errNameTaken: another file has its name on this PC
sync.errNoOtherPlace: it is on no other place; it stays
sync.errPurgatoryUnreachable: The purgatory is not reachable (its drive is unplugged); nothing was deleted.
sync.errNoPurgatoryCopy: no copy to keep in the purgatory; it stays
sync.errPurgatoryNotThis: the purgatory copy is not this photo
sync.errReadBack: The copy on the drive did not read back the same; nothing was kept.
sync.errPurgatoryReadBack: the copy on the drive did not read back the same
sync.errPhotosLiveHere: Photos live on this drive. Bring them back before forgetting it.
sync.errPurgatoryHere: The purgatory is on this drive. Move it back to this PC before forgetting it.
sync.theDriveMovedTo: the drive it was moved to
sync.errCopyNotSame: the copy on {name} is not the same; this one stays here
sync.errNoPhonePaired: No phone is paired with this computer. Pair one in Settings › Sync.
sync.errCannotAnswer: {name} cannot answer that yet: it needs the new Tetra.
sync.errNoPhoneAnswered: No phone answered. Open Tetra on the phone, on the same network as this computer.
sync.errCannotCall: {name} cannot place calls yet: it needs the new Tetra.
sync.errNeedsNewTetra: {name} needs the new Tetra for this.
